decisions.summary: Phase 1: findings snapshotted; nine Opus batches by module merged to ranking.json/ranking.md; E0 rows tiered on the brief's earlier wording get a bounded re-check (E0 only with a named page already saying what the code does); a row a dependency outranks takes that tier

decisions.summary: A second Opus reader re-tiers a 30-row sample blind; a batch disagreeing by more than one tier on more than 5 rows is re-run
decisions.why: Checks that the order the GM asked for is a reproducible estimate (spec Assumptions); it enforces the ranking, it narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Waves in tier order E0..E4; within a tier by module; a row with `after` waits for its dependency
decisions.why: 'go from easiest to hardest' (request); FR-003's ordering and SC-003's dependency clause.

decisions.summary: Waves as amendments: only the current wave's rows are task boxes; the next wave appended once a wave lands
decisions.why: FR-006 verbatim; the GM asked for one feature that keeps going.

decisions.summary: Wave 1 is every E0 row, claim lines only, no map regeneration, gate runs
decisions.why: E0 is the easiest tier, so it is first under 'easiest to hardest'; no row is excluded.

decisions.summary: Re-checks batched by module, several units per claims bundle
decisions.why: FR-003's module grouping; every row is still re-checked by impl-drift (FR-005).

decisions.summary: E4 rows take a research pass under the record's own checks before any code change
decisions.why: Spec Edge Cases (a finding the research cannot settle); the code still moves to the research afterward.

decisions.summary: A row flagged deviation-tempting goes to spec-fidelity with the request verbatim before any other fix
decisions.why: FR-004 and the Edge Cases' XVI path; the plan adds no exception of its own.

decisions.summary: Nine procedure rows that redraw a hand-drawn Mode A sheet re-tiered E1 -> E3
decisions.why: FR-003 tiers a sheet redraw E3; the rows stay in the ranking and are fixed in their tier (FR-009 names the sheets).

decisions.summary: The 32 E1 rows of hamletgen/ways/ are one wave (wave 4); FOOTPATH_FABRIC_GAP waits for it
decisions.why: FR-003's module grouping and dependency rule; nothing dropped, the rows are fixed toward 0081/0246.

decisions.summary: Waves 2+ verified on Inashiro first, then the pool through the gate, bookends, impl-drift on every touched unit
decisions.why: FR-005's verification; adds no behavior.

decisions.summary: Wave 5 is the contiguous run: row 143 (the row street) and rows 148-173, 29 rows
decisions.why: FR-006's 'contiguous run of the ranking'; the remainder is the next wave.

decisions.summary: The row street follows 0033 (runs on off the map), not 0246's clustered-lane pull-back; trim_streets no longer cuts it back
decisions.why: The implementation is moved to the page that governs a row village; the research is not changed and no row is excepted (FR-004).

decisions.summary: A town or city value no scripted map draws is proven by its unit test; bookends back to back; a held value becomes a found row
decisions.why: FR-005 regenerates the maps a wave changes; a value no map draws changes none. A held value is ranked, not dropped (Edge Cases).

decisions.summary: Closed rows keep the tier they closed at (audit/closed-tiers.json); merge.py keeps it
decisions.why: Bookkeeping of the ranking's history; it moves no open row and changes no fix.

decisions.summary: Wave 6 is the 32 open E0 rows (tasks.md Phase 7), claim lines only
decisions.why: Measured: ranking.json holds exactly 32 E0 rows with no wave, and Phase 7 lists 32; E0 is the lowest open tier (SC-003).

decisions.summary: No map regeneration, review occasion or perf bookend for wave 6
decisions.why: Claim lines change nothing a map draws; FR-005's regeneration and occasions apply to waves that change drawing, and the bookend rule to waves that change engine behavior.

decisions.summary: A claim written or relabeled never carries a code change; where the page it names answers differently from the code, the claim states the code against that page and the departure is ranked as a found row in its own tier
decisions.why: The rewording only extends the rule from relabels to claims written for UNCLAIMED units, which is the same case (Phase 7 is both). The code still moves to the research (FR-004), in the tier its work takes (FR-003, Edge Cases 'new findings a fix exposes'); the claim stays a drift, not a DEVIATION (T22 allows DEVIATION only via the exception path), so the departure stays a finding until fixed. Nothing is dropped; it is ordered, as the GM asked.

decisions.summary: Later waves take their regression baseline on the clone while its engine content is main's, before the wave's first edit
decisions.why: A verification method under constitution XIII; it does not touch the scope of what the GM asked.

decisions.summary: Before wave 7 chooses its rows, the 34 found rows tiered by verdict alone (waves 4-6 re-checks) are tiered by their work by a fresh Opus reader (audit/t25a-out.jsonl, applied in overrides.json with T25a notes); 18 moved; the folded brook-width row carried by row 203's fix
decisions.why: Measured: all 34 t25a rows sit in ranking.json at the reader's tier and fix (0 mismatches), every override carries its T25a note, and no other ranking row changed. It enforces FR-002/FR-003 (the order by work) and SC-003; the reasons spot-checked in the code hold (walls.py:432 else 12, :507 >= 45, :532 + 12.0, :540 130/55; castle_civic.py:810 bm = 32; bridges.py DEFAULT_W 9.0/4.2). The folded row's value change (brook to px(7)) is in row 203's fix, so nothing is dropped.

decisions.summary: Wave 7: the 7 open E0 rows, then the contiguous E1 run, global rows 183-234 (27 open rows, tasks.md Phase 8), ending at the civic grounds' last row; next open E1 row 235; 232 and 233 wait on 231 inside the wave
decisions.why: Measured on ranking.json after T25a: exactly 7 open E0 rows (52,53,54,56,62,98,137); the first open E1 row is 183 and rows 183-234 hold 27 open E1 rows; Phase 8 lists exactly these 34 keys (none missing, none extra); every after is inside the wave. The round-3 objections are answered: the wall literals (now 211,215,217) are in the run, the claim relabels are E0 and in the wave, the fallback seat, the river-tap sweep and the arcade moved to E2/E2/E3 and out. Tier order is monotone over the ranking. FR-006 contiguous run, SC-003 lowest tier first.

decisions.summary: Wave 7 verified as wave 5: Inashiro first (PNG looked at), the pool through the gate, a town or city value by its unit test, bookends back to back, impl-drift on every touched unit, a held value becomes a found row
decisions.why: FR-005 and the spec's Edge Case for a fix that makes a map fail (held value -> found row, recorded in the ranking); the same verification already ruled within for wave 5.

decisions.summary: Before wave 8 chooses its rows, the 14 found rows wave 7's re-checks tiered by verdict alone are tiered by their work by a fresh Opus reader (audit/t29a-out.jsonl, applied in overrides.json); 11 moved
decisions.why: FR-002/FR-003 tier by implementation work and SC-003 orders the waves by tier; the same step as T25a. Re-measured on round 2 against ranking.json at 70f7115a9: 11 of the 14 changed tier (2 to E3, 5 to E2, 1 to E4, 3 to E1), matching the plan's list; the two research gaps were E4 before and after.

decisions.summary: Under D8, each wave-8 E0 claim that states a drift names the found row that fixes it: street.py row_reach farm frame (E1, row 192), law_water oblique_at channel crossing (E4, row 713), funerary cremation_ground fire bed's two forms (E3, row 634); row 83 names consts.py::LANE_CLEARANCE (E3, row 570)
decisions.why: FR-004 moves the implementation to the research and the spec's Edge Cases record a departure as a found row in the tier its work takes; nothing is dropped - each drift is a ranked row (all four present in ranking.json), and the fire bed's two forms become a knob, as the research doctrine requires for two attested forms.

decisions.summary: Wave 8: the 18 open E0 rows, then the contiguous E1 run, global rows 187-247 (9 open rows, the farm frame at 192 included), ending at the civic grounds' last open row; next open E1 row 253
decisions.why: Measured on round 2 in ranking.json: 18 open E0 rows (48-53, 58, 61, 62, 70, 81, 83, 120-124, 153); open E1 rows before 253 are exactly 187, 192, 209, 231, 242, 243, 244, 245, 247, and tasks.md Phase 9 lists those 27 rows. Nothing between is skipped (FR-006 contiguous run, lowest tier first).

decisions.summary: Wave 8 verified as wave 7: Inashiro first, the pool through the gate, a town or city value by its unit test, bookends back to back, impl-drift on every touched unit, a held value becomes a found row
decisions.why: FR-005 and the spec's Edge Cases. The occasions line's scope checked on round 2: every scripted pool hamlet's manifest carries empty cemeteries and cremation_grounds, and the pool's other scripted wrappers rasterize hand-authored sheets.

decisions.summary: Scope from the gen cache's execution records: every (path, qualname) recorded under .gencache/*/ and .gencache/rolls/*/ is `kept` (plus classes with a run method, constants an executed function reads, KEPT_CHECKS, and buildings* as mode-a); everything else deferred
decisions.why: The unit-level measure is right and answers round 1 (crescent_pond, water_field, _grove_fits, _shades_a_garden, merchant_estate, water_gate, _try_place_legacy, nearring.py all read deferred; scope.json and claims-deferred.json reproduce exactly, 963 of 3945). But the records it reads are not the kept maps' runs. Measured on round 2: .gencache/rolls holds 32 entries, none a kept map (tests/rolls.py: the gate rolls ZERO maps of its own since feature 219): three `roll_village:*` gate-test rolls of the legacy feature-005 roller (tests/gate/settlement/test_rolling.py; no pool generator calls roll_village), seven HamletSpec rolls from older engine code (Sep 8-29, their spec repr lacks grove_sides/row_line), and unit-test field rolls. Excluding only the roll_village rolls moves 14 open rows kept->deferred (all of rolling/roll.py plus _knobs._land_use_ok); using only the kept maps' entries and current-code HamletSpec rolls moves 20, including FuneraryGroundsMixin.cemetery, which no current kept map runs (the hamlet burial stage draws nothing; only the Sep 29 rolls record it). Wave 9 takes three of these (cemetery#stupa E0, cemetery#six jizo E1, RollVillageMixin._roll_civic E1). The GM: 'limit ourselves to code actually executed by magistracies, country shrines, and scripted hamlets'. A gate test of the legacy roller and a stale record of old code are neither; the round-1 code itself called roll.py 'the legacy village roller, which no scripted hamlet runs'.

decisions.summary: dev/claims-deferred.json derived over every claimed unit (963 of 3945), re-derived when a wave lands
decisions.why: Answers round 1: measured, the list is computed over every unit of dev/claims-index.json, not today's findings, and FR-010 and the plan say it is re-run when a wave lands. Its CONTENT inherits D9-scope-rule's measure (990 with the legacy roller's rolls excluded, 1078 on current kept-map records only) and is corrected with it.

decisions.summary: A unit with any in-scope row stays in scope (never listed deferred)
decisions.why: Prevents deferring code a kept map executes; serves the GM's limit.

decisions.summary: Rows already fixed in now-deferred code (waves 5-8) stay closed; their open remainder is deferred
decisions.why: The GM: 'finish your current round of in-progress stuff, the[n] edit the feature' - nothing asks the done work undone.

decisions.summary: The cap is 85%, the hook re-armed at 85; the plan's Summary now says 85%
